title: Kahana vs Patreon: Dual Listing, Not a Migration
excerpt: Patreon is recurring membership, creator funding, exclusive posts, and a fan community built around supporting the person, often via tiered subscriptions. Kahana is library discovery and flexible hub pricing beside patronage.

columns.label: Ebook
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily get and consume ebooks on the platform (free or paid) as a first-class product, open, buy, borrow, or read without hunting.

columns.label: Short-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily consume short-form video as a first-class surface (For You, Reels, Shorts).

columns.label: Long-form video
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch creator / UGC long-form video (or specialty long video) as a core surface. Course lectures belong under Courses. Hollywood catalogs belong under Series/Films.

columns.label: Series/Films
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily watch series and films as an SVOD / catalog entertainment product.

columns.label: Courses
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily take or browse structured courses as a first-class product.

columns.label: Newsletters
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily read or subscribe to newsletters / creator writing as a first-class product.

columns.label: Audio
columns.definition: Yes if you can easily listen to music, podcasts, or audiobooks as a first-class product.

columns.label: Memberships
columns.definition: Yes if a creator or seller can accept payments from others and make money through the platform, checkout, fan subscriptions, tips, ads, shop, or creator funds. Not only a classic Patreon-style membership product.

columns.label: Community & Messaging
columns.definition: Yes if you can create or join a group, community, or club, including group chats, Groups, subreddits, community tabs, discussion boards, or community feeds. A one-off comment on a single video or listing is not the bar; a durable place for the group to talk is.

columns.label: Storefronts
columns.definition: Yes if the product gives a creator a custom storefront or site that can take the place of building their own website (bio page, creator site, branded shop). Not a shop tab on someone else’s multi-seller marketplace.

columns.label: Marketplaces
columns.definition: Yes if a typical person can search and shop a catalog of offerings from many sellers, courses, books, digital goods, etc. Storefront software (Shopify, WooCommerce) is not a marketplace unless shoppers browse many sellers there.

scaleFacts: 8M+ active patrons supporting creators as of 2024.
240k+ creators with at least one paying member; 200k+ creators have earned money via Patreon.
Creators have earned USD 3.5B+ to date, with payouts continuing to grow.
Take rate ≈5–12% of creators’ income depending on plan (Lite, Pro, Premium), plus payment processing fees.

strengths.title: Tiered membership model
strengths.detail: Multiple tiers with different prices and perks (exclusive posts, videos, Discord access, Q&A) for flexible monetization.

strengths.title: Recurring, predictable income
strengths.detail: Monthly or per-creation subscriptions create more stable revenue than one-off sales or ads.

strengths.title: Community and communication tools
strengths.detail: Native posts, messaging, polls, and Discord integration help build a private community around the creator’s work.

strengths.title: Analytics and insights
strengths.detail: Track patron growth, revenue, and churn to optimize tiers and offerings.

weaknesses.title: Platform fees and processing costs
weaknesses.detail: 5–12% commission plus processor fees can be substantial, especially at lower income levels.

weaknesses.title: Churn and tier management overhead
weaknesses.detail: Patrons can cancel anytime; creators must continuously maintain tier value and manage churn.

weaknesses.title: Limited ownership and portability
weaknesses.detail: Dependent on Patreon’s rules and policies; migrating patrons elsewhere is difficult.

weaknesses.title: Discovery not a primary strength
weaknesses.detail: Not a strong discovery engine, creators usually bring audiences from YouTube, Twitch, or social.

content:
Kahana is a library of curated hubs, Explore, Clubs, and optional Stripe. Patreon is recurring membership, creator funding, exclusive posts, and a fan community built around supporting the person, often via tiered subscriptions. They overlap in places and diverge in others.

What each one is

Kahana is built around hubs people can open, Explore so strangers can find them, Aura as scarce daily recognition, and Clubs so discussion outlives a feed. Selling stays optional.

Patreon is a membership platform that allows content creators to receive recurring payments from supporters (patrons) in exchange for exclusive content or perks.

Why this comparison

This article puts Kahana and Patreon side by side. It covers what each supports as a first-class product job, key features, and a few research notes so you have a clearer picture of what they are, how they compare, and what you can actually do on each one. It is not a teardown, and it is not a switch-tomorrow pitch.
contentAfter:
What you can do on each

On Kahana you can publish a hub, list it on Explore, discuss it in a Club, grant Aura, and turn on a Stripe paywall when you are ready to charge.

On Patreon you can use Memberships as a first-class product job. Fans already live on that membership surface and prefer tiers, posts, or patronage-native extras.

Using Kahana with Patreon

You can use both. Patreon keeps doing what it already does well. Kahana is another place to package the work, get discovered, and grow an audience.

Keep patronage-native fans on Patreon. Dual-list related work on Kahana so people who browse libraries can find it, join a Club, and pay there too without rebuilding your whole fan stack.
